result.title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
result.summary: Recent LLM-centric advances can generate attractive furnished rooms by selecting and arranging assets. Yet evaluation remains limited to specific perspectives or predefined questions, failing to reflect overall scene quality. To address this pressing need, we introduce GREP. Its core is a focus shift from defining specific questions to establishing a three-tier evaluation philosophy: basic physical validity checks whether a scene obeys physical constraints; visual coherence concerns compatibility in object scale, style, and composition; and, at the highest level, human-use logic requires object arrangements to align with everyday human habits. Guided by these principles, an evaluation agent autonomously and adaptively identifies issues from scene context, gathers evidence, and produces scores and reports. This supports scene-specific issue discovery and reliable judgments. Experiments show that (1) GREP achieves 87% agreement with human majority preferences, substantially outperforming baseline evaluators. (2) GREP reports improve scene quality through refinement, whereas score-only and no-feedback baselines show slight declines. (3) GREP suggests that as planning ability improves, recent models such as GPT-5.6 Sol can move from relying on pipelines and harnesses to challenging their guidance and constraints, but still lack the ability to resolve the resulting conflicts. Stronger models are therefore expected not only to plan well, but also to adapt to external guidance and constraints more flexibly. Project page: https://han-808.github.io/GREP/

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GREP，以物理有效性、视觉一致性、人类使用逻辑三层原则指导一个评估 agent 自主从场景上下文中定位问题、收集证据并输出评分与报告，用于评价 LLM 生成的家具房间场景，并验证反馈报告可反哺场景改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「定原则—自主找问题—取证—给判断」的分层评估流程，可能与 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、何时继续获取证据与停止的决策有概念关联，但对象是 3D 房间场景而非模型内部推理状态，具体可借鉴程度需核查。
